hand-built-transactions-refused-by-the-d.text: Hand-built transactions refused by the deployed validators on a development network.

Issue 764, first slice, part of milestone 1. This page is for a KERI integrator reading the 1.0 release, for an author of another application, and for the people who review the pull request. It records the story, the requirements, the three refusals and what the check does not show.

story.text: As a KERI integrator reading the 1.0 release, I see a hosted job on a development network in which transactions built by hand, outside the packaged commands, are refused by the deployed validators. The packaged commands decline most wrong requests before sending anything, so on their own they never show what the chain itself refuses. This job builds each wrong transaction with the repository's own transaction-building libraries, submits it to the node, and shows the validator's failure beside the same transaction built correctly and accepted.

requirements.text: taken-key-registration-refused: the node refuses a registration of a key that is already registered, by the failure of the registry's state validator, using only the answer the honest registry tree gives for that key.
update-without-controller-refused: the node refuses an update of a holding that the key's controller did not sign, by the failure of the open-datum request validator.
token-leaving-holding-refused: the node refuses a transaction that spends a holding and does not return the key's token to it, by the failure of the open-datum request validator.
each-refusal-has-a-control: beside each refusal runs the same transaction with only the one wrong fact restored, and the node accepts it and the chain records it.

refusal-read-from-the-validator: a refusal counts only when the node's answer names a validator of the application as failing by its own code (an explicit failure, not an exhausted budget) and the chain's own record does not hold the transaction. A control counts only when the chain's own record holds it.
job-reads-green-on-all-six: the job is green only when all three refusals and all three controls behave as stated, and each assertion is shown failing on altered input.

built-with-repository-libraries: the three attempts and their controls are built with the repository's transaction builders and read the chain through the ledger provider session; they use neither cardano-cli nor the packaged commands. The packaged commands only make the starting registry, key and holding.
deployed-validators-as-built: the job runs against the validators as built from main. No validator is patched.
hosted-and-counted: the job is a hosted job in the development-network workflow, with its step, and the check that declared checks are hosted accepts it.
no-change-to-scripts-model-or-wire-format: no on-chain script, script hash, Lean model or wire format changes.

assumption.text: The trie library's proofs are assumed sound.

out-of-scope.text: This ticket ports the three cases above from the first row of issue 764 only. The rest of that row and every other row stay open there: the Demo 1 journeys from the release archive, the independent-actor checks, the public-indexer readback, the one-output creation, the refusals on one existing registry beyond these three, the command recovery rows, the KERI-shaped consumer, the naming checks, the devnet parts, the conformance devnet rows and the retired model and simulator checks. The pull request says Refs #764.
